title: TokenTide microbench harness: cross-model tokens/sec & p95 drift detection
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Goal:
Build and maintain TokenTide, a reproducible microbenchmark harness that measures tokens/sec (steady-state and transient), per-request p95 latency, and model warmup behavior for Redwood core models. TokenTide will live in the perf repo, run as both a nightly suite and a lightweight CI gate for PRs touching the serving runtime or model packaging.

Scope and motivations:
- Capture realistic token throughput under multiple synthetic 'user mixes' (short, medium, long prompts) rather than a single canonical prompt.
- Track p95 and p99 tail latency alongside tokens/sec to detect regressions that trade throughput for high-latency outliers.
- Include KV-cache warmup and prefix-caching scenarios to emulate common LLM patterns and detect regressions caused by cache eviction or kernel scheduling.
- Provide automated regression detection and a bisect helper that can isolate the offending commit range when CI gates fail.
- Produce per-model baselines (tokens/sec, p95 baseline, GPU occupancy, KV hit ratio) and surface them in a Grafana dashboard with regression alerts.

Acceptance criteria:
1) TokenTide runs end-to-end on the core model matrix (redwood-small, redwood-medium, open-llama-13B) and produces stable baseline artifacts (JSON + CSV) that CI can compare against.
2) Regression detection algorithm implemented: flags a run when steady-state tokens/sec drops by >7% or p95 increases by >10% relative to baseline (configurable per-model).
3) Bisect workflow: python/bisect_regress.py automates checkout of candidate commits, runs a minimal reproducible harness, and narrows failing commit range to <=5 commits.
4) Dashboard: Grafana panel with tokens/sec trend, p95 trend, GPU util, and a toggle for KV-warm vs cold runs; alert configured to send Slack to #infra-perf.
5) CI: lightweight smokebench that runs on PRs touching runtime, fails fast (<10m) for obvious regressions and schedules full nightly run for in-depth drift checks.

Planned tasks:
- T1: Define canonical prompt set and user-mix weights (short=60%, medium=30%, long=10%). Create golden prompt corpus and upload to GCS.
- T2: Implement harness runner with steady-state detection, token counting, and warmup phase.
- T3: Instrument metrics (tokens/sec, p95/p99, GPU occupancy, KV hit ratio) and export to Prometheus-compatible endpoint.
- T4: Baseline generation job and storage of artifact manifests for CI comparisons.
- T5: Regression detector + bisect helper + PR smokebench integration.
- T6: Grafana dashboard + alerting rules + docs for oncall runbook.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Synthetic user mixes instead of live traffic capture: avoids PII and provides reproducibility, but requires careful prompt design to be representative.
- Thresholds (7% tokens/sec, 10% p95) chosen from historical noise analysis on the token-rate corpus; will be tunable per-model and per-hardware class.
- CI gate split: fast smokebench for immediate feedback; nightly full suite to reduce flakiness and avoid blocking.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for end-to-end customer traffic regression tests. TokenTide is a fast, reproducible lab-first signal.
- Not attempting to model multi-tenant interference at scale; that is a separate capacity testing project.

Operational notes:
- Harness should be deterministic given a seed and workload file. Randomness limited to jitter for concurrency testing.
- Store baselines in gs://redwood-perf/baselines/tokenTide/{model}/{hardware}/{date}/manifest.json.
- Nightly runs write artifacts and trigger post-run artifact delta checks. A failing nightly opens ENG ticket with first-failure artifacts attached.

Links to artifacts and prior work:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/TokenTide+Microbench+Design
- Golden prompt corpus (GCS): gs://redwood-perf/golden-prompts/tokentide-v1.tar.gz
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf/pull/4125
- Existing baseline job for throughput: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/steady-state?orgId=1

Notes on model coverage:
- Initial phase targets 3 core models on dedicated A100/80GB pools. Phase 2 adds quantized variants and Llama-family models in dedicated and hosted flavors.
